title: Site Reliability Engineer, Cells Infrastructure
description:
GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100\* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

* *Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.*

**An overview of this role**
----------------------------

We're looking for an Intermediate Site Reliability Engineer to join the Cells Infrastructure team in GitLab's Scale & Architecture organization. In this role, you'll help build and operate Cells, the architecture that lets GitLab.com scale horizontally. Cells splits GitLab.com into many independent units, each with its own application and data stack, behind a shared routing layer.

This is a build-it-and-run-it role. You'll provision cells, route traffic to them, deploy them safely, and keep them reliable in production. You'll also help move customer organizations onto Cells, one of GitLab's most important scaling initiatives.

**What you'll do**
------------------

* Operate Cells in production: join the on-call rotation, respond to incidents, lead post-incident reviews, and drive corrective actions to completion.
* Define and monitor service level objectives (SLOs) for routing and cell health, and build the dashboards, alerts, and runbooks behind them.
* Provision and operate cell infrastructure on Amazon Web Services (AWS) and Google Cloud Platform (GCP), including Kubernetes, networking, Identity and Access Management (IAM), PostgreSQL, Redis, and object storage.
* Develop infrastructure as code with Terraform, Helm, and GitOps tooling such as Argo CD.
* Operate and extend the global routing layer, built on Cloudflare Workers, Envoy, and a Go service backed by Cloud Spanner, and expand routing to more protocols and services.
* Improve the continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) pipelines behind ring-based deployments, covering promotion, database migrations, quality assurance validation, and rollback.
* Support organization migrations by preparing destination cells and helping with dry runs and production cutovers.
* Work with product teams to make their services cell-compatible, and write documentation so others can operate Cells with confidence.

**What you'll bring**
---------------------

* Professional experience running production infrastructure at scale on AWS, GCP, or both, including Kubernetes, along with strong Terraform and Helm skills.
* Proficiency in Go, or strong experience in another systems language and willingness to work in Go daily.
* Solid grounding in site reliability engineering (SRE) best practices: SLOs and error budgets, blameless post-incident reviews, reducing toil through automation, capacity planning, and designing for graceful degradation.
* Experience owning services in production, including on-call, incident response, and monitoring with tools such as Prometheus and Grafana.
* Practical knowledge of progressive delivery: how to roll changes safely across a fleet and how to roll them back.
* A strong understanding of distributed-systems fundamentals, such as request routing, proxies, consistency, and failure domains.
* Experience working effectively in distributed, all-remote teams: you default to asynchronous, written-first communication, document decisions in issues and merge requests, hand off work cleanly across time zones, and stay transparent about progress and blockers.
* Experience with Cloudflare, Spanner, Argo CD, TypeScript, or operating GitLab at scale is a plus, not a requirement.

**About the team**
------------------

Every team in our organization owns its services end to end, from design through on-call.We own the control plane that tracks cells and decides where each request belongs, and keep the fleet in step with GitLab's release cadence.We work closely with delivery, database, migration, and product teams across GitLab. Feature teams own how their services behave on the platform; we own the underlying infrastructure.We're an all-remote, asynchronous team. We make decisions in GitLab issues, use directly responsible individuals (DRIs) to own technical direction, demo our work weekly, and use AI-assisted workflows every day.

#### **How GitLab Supports Full-Time Employees**

* Benefits to support your health, finances, and well-being
* Flexible Paid Time Off
* Team Member Resource Groups
* Equity Compensation & Employee Stock Purchase Plan
* Growth and Development Fund
* Parental Leave

Please note that we welcome interest from candidates with varying levels of experience; many successful candidates do not meet every single requirement. Additionally, studies have shown that people from underrepresented groups are less likely to apply to a job unless they meet every single qualification. If you're excited about this role, please apply and allow our recruiters to assess your application.

**Country Hiring Guidelines:** GitLab hires new team members in countries around the world. All of our roles are remote, however some roles may carry specific location-based eligibility requirements. Our Talent Acquisition team can help answer any questions about location after starting the recruiting process.

**Privacy Policy:** Please review our Recruitment Privacy Policy. Your privacy is important to us.

GitLab is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and is an affirmative action employer. GitLab’s policies and practices relating to recruitment, employment, career development and advancement, promotion, and retirement are based solely on merit, regardless of race, color, religion, ancestry, sex (including pregnancy, lactation, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression), national origin, age, citizenship, marital status, mental or physical disability, genetic information (including family medical history), discharge status from the military, protected veteran status (which includes disabled veterans, recently separated veterans, active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans, and Armed Forces service medal veterans), or any other basis protected by law. GitLab will not tolerate discrimination or harassment based on any of these characteristics. See also GitLab’s EEO Policy and EEO is the Law. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know during the recruiting process.

title: Senior Staff Site Reliability Engineer
description:
**Date posted** 10/13/2026

### **Category** **Information Technology****Hire Type** **Employee****Job ID** **18874****Remote Eligible** **No****Date Posted** **10/13/2026**

**We Are**

Synopsys is the leader in engineering solutions from silicon to systems, enabling customers to rapidly innovate AI-powered products. We deliver industry-leading silicon design, IP, simulation and analysis solutions, and design services. We partner closely with our customers across a wide range of industries to maximize their R&D capability and productivity, powering innovation today that ignites the ingenuity of tomorrow.

  
  

**You Are**

You have spent a decade building systems that need to stay up, not just run, actually stay up, under production load with real users depending on them. You know that observability is not about dashboards that look good in demos, it is about catching the signal before the page goes out at 2am. You think in SLOs and error budgets because you have lived through enough incidents to know that hope is not a strategy.

You are the person who walks into a war room, pulls up three graphs, and knows exactly which service is choking and why. Linux is your native language. You have written enough Bash and Python to automate yourself out of repetitive work, and you know when to reach for Terraform or Ansible to make infrastructure repeatable. Cloud platforms like Azure do not intimidate you because you have built on them, broken things on them, and fixed them under pressure.

EDA workloads are not abstract to you. You have worked with Grid Engine, LSF, or SLURM. You understand what it means when a compute-heavy job grid starts behaving strangely, and you know how to instrument it. Elasticsearch, Prometheus, Grafana, these are not buzzwords, they are tools you have deployed, tuned, and scaled.

At Synopsys, you will build the observability backbone that keeps our Cloud and on-prem production systems visible, reliable, and ready for what comes next.

  
  

**What You'll Be Doing**

Design, build, and own the SRE and Observability platform that monitors production systems across on-prem and Azure Cloud environments, giving engineering and operations teams a real-time, holistic view of system health

Partner with product, infrastructure, and application teams to define SLAs, SLIs, SLOs, error budgets, and KPIs that actually matter, then instrument systems to track them

Automate deployment and configuration of monitoring tools using Terraform, Ansible, Bash, and Python to eliminate manual toil and reduce configuration drift

Build custom scripts and tooling to extend observability capabilities, including proactive remediation workflows and self-healing automation that catches issues before they become incidents

Lead root cause analysis on production incidents, write detailed postmortems for stakeholders, and drive systemic fixes that prevent recurrence

Mentor junior SREs and Cloud Operations engineers, providing technical guidance on Linux systems, observability tooling, and SRE best practices

Evaluate, test, and integrate new observability and reliability tools and technologies, including AI-assisted monitoring, copilots, and emerging patterns like MCP and RAG

  
  

**The Impact You Will Have**

Production systems across Synopsys Cloud will be more visible, more reliable, and easier to debug because of the observability platform you build

Engineering teams will spend less time firefighting and more time building because your automation catches problems early and fixes them without human intervention

Incident response times will drop because the right data will be surfaced at the right time, and teams will know what to look at first

SRE practices will become embedded across the organization as you define KPIs, error budgets, and reliability standards that other teams adopt

Junior engineers will grow faster because you will teach them how to think about reliability, not just react to alerts

The Cloud Operations team will scale more effectively because repeatable, automated workflows replace one-off manual fixes

Stakeholders will have confidence in production stability because postmortems and reliability metrics will be clear, honest, and actionable

  
  

**What You'll Need**

10+ years of hands-on experience in software development, system administration, or site reliability engineering with a focus on production systems

Deep expertise in Linux OS internals, networking, and NFS technologies, you should be able to troubleshoot kernel-level issues and performance bottlenecks

Strong experience with Elasticsearch for log aggregation and search, this is non-negotiable for the role

Solid programming and scripting skills in Bash and Python, with proven ability to build automation that runs in production

Hands-on experience with infrastructure as code using Terraform and configuration management using Ansible

Expertise in at least one major cloud platform, Azure strongly preferred, AWS or GCP also relevant

Experience working with EDA workloads and job schedulers like Grid Engine, LSF, or SLURM in production environments, experience with Prometheus and Grafana is a strong plus, familiarity with Docker, Swarm, or Kubernetes is helpful but not required

  
  

**Who You Are**

You have a proactive mindset, you spot performance bottlenecks and reliability risks before they become incidents, and you act on them without being asked

You can explain a complex system failure to a VP in two sentences without losing the technical nuance, and you can write a postmortem that engineers and executives both find useful

You are comfortable working across teams, you know how to pull the right data from product engineers, negotiate SLOs with stakeholders, and get buy-in for automation projects

You do not need perfect requirements to move forward, you ask the right questions, make reasonable assumptions, document them, and iterate as you learn more

You care about the details, monitoring configurations, alert thresholds, dashboard layouts, because you know that small mistakes in observability tooling create big problems downstream

You are someone who mentors by doing, you pair with junior engineers, review their scripts, and show them how to think through reliability tradeoffs in real time

  
  

**The Team You'll Be Part Of**

You will join the Synopsys Cloud infrastructure team, a group responsible for the reliability and observability of production systems running on Azure, GCP, AWS. This team builds the infrastructure that keeps EDA workloads running at scale, and your work will directly support engineering teams across the company who depend on stable, visible, and well-instrumented systems.

  
  

**Rewards and Benefits**

We offer a comprehensive range of health, wellness, and financial benefits to cater to your needs. Our total rewards include both monetary and non-monetary offerings. Your recruiter will provide more details about the salary range and benefits during the hiring process.

At Synopsys, we want talented people of every background to feel valued and supported to do their best work. Synopsys considers all applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, military veteran status, or disability.

description:
As a global leader in cybersecurity, CrowdStrike protects the people, processes and technologies that drive modern organizations. Since 2011, our mission hasn’t changed — we’re here to stop breaches, and we’ve redefined modern security with the world’s most advanced AI-native platform. Our customers span all industries, and they count on CrowdStrike to keep their businesses running, their communities safe and their lives moving forward. We're proud to work for a mission-driven company leveraging AI to transform the way we work. CrowdStrikers drive their careers through flexibility and autonomy while also being expected to contribute to a culture of responsible AI adoption, experimentation, and innovation. We use an AI-first mindset as a force multiplier to proactively and continuously accelerate execution, build expertise, uncover insights, and solve complex problems. We’re always looking to add talented CrowdStrikers to the team who have limitless passion, a relentless focus on innovation and a fanatical commitment to our customers, our community and each other. Ready to join a mission that matters? The future of cybersecurity starts with you.

**About the Role:**

CrowdStrike is hiring an Engineer III to join the Kubernetes Platform team supporting the continued global expansion of the Falcon platform. You will be a key member of our India-based coverage for the Kubernetes environments that run CrowdStrike services across our own data centers and public clouds. We're looking for a highly technical, hands-on engineer with solid Kubernetes operating experience who can independently own platform support and improvement work, handle production incidents during India hours, and help grow less experienced engineers on the team.

**What You'll Do:**

  

* Independently operate and support large-scale Kubernetes clusters across custom data centers and public clouds (AWS, GCP, OCI), owning their availability, health, and lifecycle
* Serve as a primary responder for platform incidents during India hours — diagnosing complex node, networking, DNS, storage, and control-plane issues, driving them to resolution, and handing off cleanly across time zones
* Plan and execute cluster upgrades, add-on rollouts, and capacity changes end to end, including risk assessment, testing, and rollback planning
* Improve the reliability of the platform: identify recurring issues and technical debt, propose fixes, and see them through
* Design, build, and improve monitoring, alerting, and dashboards with Prometheus, Thanos, Alertmanager, and Grafana so problems are caught before customers notice
* Develop automation and tooling in Go to eliminate toil, and contribute to Kubernetes controllers and operators used by the team
* Evaluate open-source tools and Kubernetes add-ons and help integrate them into existing workflows
* Use AI technologies to streamline operational workflows, accelerate troubleshooting, and improve decision-making
* Write design docs, runbooks, and post-incident reviews that are clear to engineers, on-call responders, and stakeholders
* Mentor Engineer I and II team members through pairing, code review, and design review, and take part in interviewing new team members

**What You'll Need:**

  

* 5+ years of experience in infrastructure, systems, or platform engineering, including 3+ years operating production Kubernetes clusters at scale
* Strong understanding of Kubernetes internals and operations: control plane (API server, etcd, scheduler), kubelet and container runtime, networking/CNI, DNS, storage, and upgrades
* Experience with Prometheus, Thanos, Alertmanager, and Grafana
* Proficiency in Go; Python a plus
* Experience with large-scale, business-critical Linux environments
* Experience operating in at least one public cloud (AWS, GCP, or OCI) and in on-premises or custom data centers
* Experience with infrastructure as code and deployment tooling (e.g., Terraform, Ansible, Helm, GitOps) and version control with git
* Familiarity and ability to manage on-call shifts [aligned to India business hours]
* Demonstrated experience using AI technologies to enhance decision-making, streamline workflows and processes, and improve efficiency
* Proven experience utilizing AI technologies to enhance decision-making, streamline workflows and processes, improve efficiency and drive business outcomes.

**Bonus Points:**

  

* Experience writing Kubernetes operators or controllers
* Experience operating Kubernetes on bare metal
* Experience deploying microservices
* Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) or Certified Kubernetes Application Developer (CKAD)
* Experience mentoring or onboarding other engineers
* Proven ability to work effectively with both local and remote teams across time zones
* Rock solid communication skills, verbal and written
* A combination of confidence and independence…with the prudence to know when to ask for help from the rest of the team

title: Staff SRE Engineer - Voice Core Platform
description:
**Company Description**

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. That moment inspired Fred to build a company that could do that for everyone—freeing people from busywork so they could focus on meaningful work. Today, ServiceNow is the AI control tower for business reinvention. Our ServiceNow AI platform brings together any AI, any data, and any workflow— helping 85% of the Fortune 500® work smarter, faster, and better. We're building an AI-native culture where technology and talent are unstoppable together. And we're just getting started.

Join us to put AI to work for people.

 **Job Description**

**About the role**

We are building a real-time conversational AI voice platform. An orchestrator runs every call through Voice Activity Detection, Speech-to-Text, LLM-based agent matching, tool calling against ServiceNow platform (Glide) APIs, and Text-to-Speech.

In voice, latency and reliability are the product. You will own the platform's reliability, performance and operational architecture, and set direction across teams.

**What you'll do**

* Define and drive SLIs/SLOs for availability, perceived latency (end-of-speech to first audio), and call quality.
* Instrument end-to-end tracing across every pipeline stage, and lead architectural work to cut latency.
* Design autoscaling and capacity plans for stateful, real-time connections (WebSocket, WebRTC, SIP/RTP).
* Lead load, soak and breakpoint testing, and turn results into capacity models.
* Build resilience for LLM, STT and TTS dependencies: failover, fallbacks, rate-limit handling and graceful degradation.
* Own Kubernetes architecture, infrastructure-as-code and CI/CD with safe progressive delivery.
* Lead incident response and postmortems, and mentor engineers across the team.

  
**Qualifications**

**To be successful in this role you have:**

* Experience in leveraging or critically thinking about how to integrate AI into work processes, decision-making, or problem-solving. This may include using AI-powered tools, automating workflows, analyzing AI-driven insights, or exploring AI’s potential impact on the function or industry.
* 8+ years in SRE, DevOps, production engineering or software engineering on production systems at scale.
* 1+ year building or operating real-time voice systems (VoIP, SIP/RTP, WebRTC, or STT/TTS integration).
* 2+ years building or operating AI agentic systems and orchestration pipelines (agent routing, tool calling, multi-step LLM workflows).
* 1+ year deploying and operating LLMs in production (model serving, inference optimization, provider integration and failover).
* Strong expertise in Kubernetes, cloud infrastructure ([AWS / Azure / GCP]) and Terraform or similar.
* Hands-on observability experience (OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, Grafana, Datadog or similar).
* Proficiency in Python, Go or Java.

**Nice to have**

* Experience Inference serving experience (vLLM, Triton, GPU scheduling).
* Familiarity with the ServiceNow platform or enterprise SaaS backends.

 **Additional Information**

**Work Personas**

We approach our distributed world of work with flexibility and trust. Learn more here. To determine eligibility for a work persona, ServiceNow may confirm the distance between your primary residence and the closest ServiceNow office using a third-party service.
